window._comment: RS3 NXT. WM_CLASS survives title changes and skips the Steam launcher window.

_regions_help: anchor + dx,dy offset from that corner + fixed w,h. RS3 pins panels to edges at fixed size rather than scaling them, so this survives a window resize. Negative dx/dy measure inward from a right/bottom edge.

metrics_xp._note: XP and XP/h number rows in the Metrics panel

chat_tail._note: most recent ~32 lines of All Chat. h=650 measured, not guessed: pickpocketing produces ~2 chat lines every 2s, and at h=375 a line's median visible lifetime was only 11s (max 23.8s). Rare drops and the yellow stun notice were scrolling off between clean OCR passes, so the taller region roughly doubles the number of chances to read each line. w=600 because text ends near x=560; the earlier 500 clipped lines mid-word and hid item names entirely.

backpack._note: full backpack panel. grid is relative to the region's top-left; verified against a hand count of 24 occupied slots

session_timer._note: Elapsed-time readout at the bottom of the Metrics panel, between the settings/reset buttons on the left and pause on the right. Measured against a 3840x2058 window; re-check with `shot session_timer` if the Metrics panel is moved or resized. Verified 10/10 clean OCR parses over 30s, ticking monotonically.

activity_icon._note: Skill icon shown at top-centre while XP is being gained - a dark disc with an orange progress ring. Measured on a 3840x2058 window; the ring pixel count was flat at 328 across dx -20..+10, so the framing has ~30px of tolerance. Re-check with `shot activity_icon` at a different resolution.

rules.name: pack_nearly_full
rules.alert_body: {free} slots left. The loot is winning; bank soon.
rules._note: Advance warning: fires when the projected time-to-full drops under lead_seconds. Paired with pack_filling, which is the overflow backstop - this one says 'about to fill', that one says 'already full and idle'. Distinct sounds so they are told apart without looking. lead_seconds=15 against a measured mean transit of 23s and a fill rate of ~19 slots/min. cooldown=55 is just under the 73s mean cycle, so it fires at most once per bank trip. EXPECT roughly one alert per trip: that is the cost of advance warning at this cycle length - switch this rule off if it becomes noise again. log_occupancy=false because pack_filling owns the log; two writers would double every transition and corrupt `watcher.py stats`.

rules.name: pack_filling
rules.alert_body: Pack full for {stuck:.0f}s. Thieving has stopped, with admirable efficiency.
rules._note: Overflow mode, not lead-time. Measured over 12 cycles with `watcher.py stats`: mean cycle 73s, mean peak 27.0/28. A predictive warning therefore fired once per bank trip - ~50 alerts an hour - while the stats showed the trips were already being banked correctly without it. Overflow only fires once the pack has been full for overflow_seconds, which is the point where catches are genuinely being lost. Set mode to 'lead' with lead_seconds to go back to predictive warning; that suits a slow grind (mining, woodcutting) where the walk to the bank is long relative to the fill.

rules.name: xp_stalled
rules._threshold_note: measured: static floor 0.001, XP tick 1.3-4.0. No mask - the Metrics panel is opaque, and a brightness mask only added antialiasing flicker.
rules.alert_body: No XP for {still:.0f}s. The grind has entered its contemplative phase.
rules._disabled_note: Superseded by fishing_stopped, which detects the same event from chat in 30s instead of 60s. Two rules firing for one spot move is just double beeping. Metrics XP is also the weaker signal: it stalls identically whether the spot moved, the client was minimised, or the panel was closed. Re-enable for a grind with no per-action chat message, where XP is the only evidence of progress.

rules.name: impling
rules.pattern: a creature is discovered while skilling|an impling (has )?appear
rules.alert_body: An impling appeared. Naturally, while you were busy stealing.
rules._note: Implings spawn silently and despawn; the message is easy to miss mid-grind. Rare enough to deserve its own sound - message-highlight is distinct from the warning tones used by pack_filling and xp_stalled, so it is recognisable without looking. Long timeout because the impling despawns: the popup should still be on screen when you glance over.
rules._disabled_note: Implings spawn from skilling, but the message was only verified during fishing. Re-enable once confirmed it appears while thieving - the pattern itself ('A creature is discovered while skilling') is already proven correct in live chat.

rules.name: level_up
rules.alert_body: Level up. The game noticed your progress before you did.

rules.name: thieving_stopped
rules.pattern: you pick the target'?s pocket|camouflage outfit keeps you hidden|coins have been added to your money pouch
rules.suppress_pattern: can'?t carry any more|do not have any space in your inventory|not have any space
rules.alert_body: No pickpocketing for {quiet:.0f}s. The target, at least, is enjoying this.
rules._note: Fires when ALL evidence of pickpocketing stops. VERIFIED wording from live chat. The pattern uses three independent activity signals: the pickpocket success line, the money-pouch line, and the camouflage-outfit line. OCR of this font degrades badly when a busy 3D scene shows through the semi-transparent chat panel (observed 'ACE rrire aasws Bamrs'), and with only the success line this rule fired 4 times in 3 minutes while pickpocketing was demonstrably continuing - the coin counter advanced throughout. Any of the three activity lines proves progress. stop_seconds=45 (up from 20) because a stun alone pauses gains for ~3s and a garbled OCR run can hide several polls; 45s still leaves room for transient unreadability. The stun notice is deliberately excluded: being stunned is evidence of a halt, and counting it kept the stop timer alive through a genuine stop.
rules._disabled_note: Superseded by activity_icon_gone, which uses the top-centre skill icon as the primary signal and chat as corroboration during icon blackouts. This avoids inferring a stop solely from missing OCR lines while still protecting against false icon absences. Re-enable this chat-only rule for a skill or layout where the activity icon cannot be monitored reliably.

rules.name: target_alerted
rules.alert_body: The target noticed. Subtlety remains theoretical.
rules._note: VERIFIED from live chat: 'Your pickpocket target becomes aware of your presence.', rendered in yellow. This is a WARNING, not a stop - pickpocketing continues through it. Kept separate from the stun rule because the two have different consequences and deserve different sounds. Per the wiki, success is 100% only for the first ~43s (25 attempts) before decaying, so this is expected rather than exceptional; cooldown=30 collapses a run into one alert.

rules.name: loot_drop
rules.item_pattern: extra fine sand|acadia wood spirit|waterskin|potato cactus|vital spark|large bladed adamant salvage|menaphite gift offering \(small\)|menaphite gift offering \(medium\)|menaphite gift offering|sealed clue scroll \(master\)|sealed clue scroll \(elite\)|sealed clue scroll \(hard\)|sealed clue scroll
rules.ignore_pattern: coins have been added|you pick the target|camouflage outfit keeps
rules.alert_body: Loot: {item}. The economy survives another drop.
rules._note: Announces a named item drop and ignores the currency line. Item list taken from the RuneScape Wiki drop table for Menaphos market guards: coins 758/1000, extra fine sand 100/1000, acadia wood spirit 50/1000, waterskin 50/1000, large bladed adamant salvage 20/1000, sealed clue (hard) 6/1000, menaphite gift offering small 4/1000, potato cactus 5/1000, vital spark 2/1000, gift offering medium 2/1000, sealed clue (elite) ~495/100000, master 5/100000. Coins are excluded because they land in the money pouch roughly every two seconds and would bury the rare drops. cooldown=0 because every drop is worth seeing; the alternatives in the pattern are ordered longest-first so '(elite)' wins over the bare 'sealed clue scroll'.
rules._disabled_note: Superseded by item_gained, which watches the backpack instead of chat. The inventory is the stronger signal: a dropped item is simply present, whereas chat lines survive a measured median of only 11s before scrolling off and the chat font OCRs poorly over a busy 3D scene. Re-enable if the exact item NAME matters more than reliable detection - this rule can name the item, while item_gained can only say which slot grew.

rules.name: coin_milestone
rules.pattern: (\d[\d,]*)\s*coins have been added to your money pouch
rules.alert_body: {total} coins pickpocketed. {n}M milestone reached; capitalism remains operational.
rules._note: Sums the money-pouch line and alerts once per million. Coins go straight to the pouch, which the backpack grid cannot see, so chat is the only evidence. At 455 coins per success and ~76% success rate that is roughly 2,900 pickpockets per million, so milestone-based alerting is essential - per-gain would fire every two seconds. The running total is persisted to state/counters.jsonl and restored on startup, so a restart mid-grind does not rewind progress.

rules.name: stunned
rules.pattern: you'?ve been stunned|you have been stunned|you are stunned|you fail to steal from the target
rules.alert_body: Stunned. The target has filed a formal objection.
rules._note:
VERIFIED from live chat - the real failure path is TWO lines, one second apart:
  [21:03:25] You fail to steal from the target.
  [21:03:26] You've been stunned.
Both are matched because OCR often catches only one of them. The earlier guessed pattern used 'you (have been |are )?stunned' and 'you fail to pick', and missed BOTH real lines: the game uses the contraction "You've" and says 'fail to steal from the target', not 'fail to pick'. Per the wiki a stun lasts 5 ticks (~3s) and deals 200 + 3% of base life points, and it halts pickpocketing - which is why this is a separate, louder alert than target_alerted. cooldown=25 keeps a bad streak to one alert while still reporting a later independent stun.

rules.name: item_gained
rules.alert_body: New item in {where}. The backpack has opinions.
rules._note: Detects a drop by watching stack-count digits in the backpack rather than chat. Reading the digit VALUE was tried and abandoned - tesseract got only 5 of 9 slots right even after tuning the crop, bleeding adjacent cells together into values like 1271. Counting yellow digit PIXELS instead is far steadier: measured drift on an unchanging stack is +/-2, while a real quantity change moves it 7-24, so stack_tolerance=3 sits clear of the noise. confirm_seconds=4 rejects tooltips: hovering the backpack draws one over neighbouring cells and was observed making occupancy oscillate 9/10/11 with signatures that jumped and reverted within seconds, whereas a real drop holds. Frames reading above capacity are dropped as interface overlays, same as the inventory rules. TUNED AFTER LIVE MEASUREMENT: at ~2s per pickpocket and a 10% extra-fine-sand rate, an existing stack grows roughly every 20s - measured median gap was 24s, which is genuine but far too frequent to be useful. new_slot_only=true reports only an item landing in a previously EMPTY slot, which is what a first-of-its-kind drop looks like; routine top-ups of a stack you already carry are counted silently. cooldown=120 bounds the rest.

rules.name: session_hour
rules.alert_body: Thieving for {label} ({elapsed}). Still technically a plan.
rules._note: Reads the Metrics panel's own elapsed timer rather than tracking wall-clock time in the watcher. That is the better source: it is the number the player is already reading, it pauses when they pause it, and it survives a watcher restart because the game owns it. step=3600 fires once per hour. The parser anchors on [0-5] for the minute and second fields so a garbled frame like '00:82:09' is rejected rather than becoming a bogus elapsed time, and a timer reset rewinds the milestone counter so a fresh session starts clean.

rules.name: activity_icon_gone
rules.alert_body: No activity icon for {gone:.0f}s. Thieving has stopped, pending appeal.
rules._note: Fires when the top-centre activity icon disappears AND chat shows no pickpocketing. The icon alone is not sufficient - MEASURED over a live session it was absent for 19% of samples, including one unbroken 60s stretch, while pickpocketing continued throughout: 33 pickpocket chat lines were observed during absences. The icon tracks XP-gain popups, which lapse while moving between targets or when the camera changes, so absence means 'no XP right now', not 'the activity ended'. corroborate_region therefore requires chat to agree before a stop is reported. absent_seconds=75 clears the observed 60s blackout with margin. Ring separation itself is still absolute: 328-331 present vs 0-113 scenery, so present_above=200 needs no tuning.
rules.corroborate_pattern: you pick the target'?s pocket|coins have been added to your money pouch|camouflage outfit keeps you hidden

_notification_note: Rules use urgency 'normal' with an explicit timeout_ms so KDE auto-dismisses them. Setting urgency to 'critical' makes KDE keep the popup until it is closed by hand and ignore timeout_ms - only do that for an alert you must not miss.
